card.title: Obey Without Explanation
card.instruction: Create increasingly inconvenient requests that test whether someone accepts your authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave your desk and stand by that open window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to know whether my team follows a direct request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's freezing. Can I get my coat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Fetch mine too, then come back and hold it while I check the rest of the team.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 disruptive standing order tests control, A3 explicitly names obedience and A5 adds personal coat service to B's request for warmth.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 why prompts A3 test rationale; B4 cold and coat request cause A5 extra fetching and holding duties.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks a fair question and B4 names actual discomfort with a practical remedy.

heightening.evidence: B4 relief request is permitted only with A5 a larger service burden and return to the uncomfortable location.

specificity.evidence: A1 desk to open window and B4 freezing establish the inconvenience being imposed.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 holding A's coat while the rest are checked turns self-protection into more subordinate work.

coach2.situation: A1 desk to open window and B4 freezing establish the inconvenience being imposed.
coach2.stated: B4 open-window cold fits A1 location; A5 checking others is a proposed next action, not an unseen team event.
coach2.inferred: Team leader and person under an obedience test.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 asks why A1 relocation is needed.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 states that following a direct request is the point.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 reports cold and requests permission to fetch a coat.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 expands B4 permission into fetching and holding A's coat before resuming the test.
